title: Data representation
examples: How is a letter like 'A' stored in a computer?
What is the difference between ASCII and Unicode?
If I record a song, how does the computer store the sound?

explain.say: Today we learn how computers store all kinds of information.

items: Computers use only two digits: one or zero.
This system is called the binary system.
Every piece of data is broken into these bits.

explain.say: We can represent letters using character codes like ASCII.
Unicode is a larger system that handles many more languages.
Images are stored by recording colour values for many tiny dots.
Sound waves are captured by measuring air pressure changes over time.
File size depends on the data type and the bit depth used.

faq.q: What is the main difference between ASCII and Unicode?
faq.a: ASCII uses a small set of characters for basic English letters. Unicode is much larger and can represent characters from almost every language in the world.
asks: Why do we need Unicode if ASCII exists?

faq.q: How does a computer store the sound of my voice?
faq.a: It records the sound by taking many measurements of the air pressure many times per second. This process is called sampling.
asks: Does the sample rate affect the sound quality?
What is sampling in digital audio?

faq.q: What makes an image file large or small?
faq.a: The size depends on the number of pixels and how much colour information is stored for each pixel. High resolution means more pixels.
asks: Is resolution the same as file size?
How many colours can one pixel have?

faq.q: If I save a document as a plain text file, why is it small?
faq.a: Because plain text only stores the characters themselves using simple codes like ASCII. It does not store formatting or colours.
asks: Does a Word document use more space?
What is the smallest file type?

faq.q: Do all file types use the same units of measurement?
faq.a: No, we measure bits, bytes, kilobytes, megabytes, and gigabytes. A byte is usually eight bits long.
asks: What is the relationship between bits and bytes?
Is a gigabyte bigger than a megabyte?

facts: ASCII uses 7 bits to represent 128 characters.
Unicode uses a much larger number of bits to support global languages.
Image quality is related to pixel count and colour depth.
Sound recording quality depends on the sampling rate and bit depth.

quiz.say: A simple text file containing only the word 'Hi' is represented by:

options.show: A number based on the highest possible bit depth.
options.say: A number based on the highest possible bit depth.

options.show: A number based on the sound sampling rate.
options.say: A number based on the sound sampling rate.

options.show: A small, fixed number of bytes based on character codes.
options.say: A small, fixed number of bytes based on character codes.

options.show: A large number of bytes representing the screen size.
options.say: A large number of bytes representing the screen size.

quiz.why: Text files only store characters using simple codes like ASCII or Unicode, which takes up very little space.

wrong.0: This is too much information; text files do not need high colour depth.
wrong.1: This confuses text data with audio data entirely.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because the size depends only on the characters, not the screen.

quiz.say: If you increase the sampling rate of an audio recording, what happens?

options.show: The file size will decrease significantly.
options.say: The file size will decrease significantly.

options.show: The recording will only capture louder sounds.
options.say: The recording will only capture louder sounds.

options.show: The sound will become completely silent.
options.say: The sound will become completely silent.

options.show: The recording can capture higher frequency sounds accurately.
options.say: The recording can capture higher frequency sounds accurately.

quiz.why: A higher sampling rate means more measurements of the air pressure per second, allowing for better high-frequency detail.

wrong.0: Increasing the rate means more data points, so the file size will increase.
wrong.1: The sampling rate affects frequency detail, not just the overall loudness.
wrong.2: The rate measures detail; it does not remove the actual sound content.

quiz.say: Which factor contributes most to a large image file size?

options.show: Compressing the file using only sound algorithms.
options.say: Compressing the file using only sound algorithms.

options.show: A high number of pixels and a high colour bit depth.
options.say: A high number of pixels and a high colour bit depth.

options.show: Using only the ASCII standard for colours.
options.say: Using only the ASCII standard for colours.

options.show: Recording the image at a low frame rate.
options.say: Recording the image at a low frame rate.

quiz.why: More pixels means more dots to store, and higher bit depth means more colour information for each dot.

wrong.0: Compression algorithms are specific to the type of data, like image or sound.
wrong.2: ASCII is for text, not for storing the complex colour data of an image.
wrong.3: Frame rate is for video, not for a single static image file.
